title: Child's striped mittens
subtitle: Two-colour striped mittens for children, worked in the round.
excerpt: Full mittens in two colours of DK wool for children, with a 1×1 ribbed cuff, a striped stocking stitch body, and an afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 14 and 16 cm (child small and child medium).
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 3rd series (1880s), §Children's mittens. The striped child's mitten with ribbed cuff appears in several Victorian home-knitting publications including Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870), §Knitted gloves for children.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 14 cm (child small) and 16 cm (child medium) with 1 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working across the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a large loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Child's striped mittens in two colours of DK wool, worked in the round, sized to fit hand circumferences of 14 cm (child small) and 16 cm (child medium).
The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop
on a long circular. The stripes are worked in 4-round bands, changing colour at the beginning of the round. The thumb uses the
afterthought thumb

method so the stripe sequence is not interrupted by thumb-gusset increases. Budget about 50 g per colour (110 m / 120 yards each) for both mittens. These wash well in a child's laundry routine when knitted in a superwash wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn A (main colour)
items.qty: 50 g (about 110 m / 120 yards) of DK-weight superwash wool

items.name: Yarn B (contrast colour)
items.qty: 50 g (about 110 m / 120 yards) of the same yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2 — one for the beginning of the round, one to mark the thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb marker

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. Child's mittens are sized closely, so swatch and check before casting on. At 23 stitches per 10 cm, the small mitten will be about 0.5 cm narrower at the palm. That is workable, but a 14 cm child's hand will find the fit noticeably tighter.
Stripe sequence
Work 4 rounds in colour A, then 4 rounds in colour B. Repeat throughout the body. Carry the unused colour loosely up the inside of the work, catching it every 4 rounds to avoid long floats.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Stitch counts read small (medium) for hand circumferences 14 (16) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using colour A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 30 (34) stitches. For 34 stitches at 3.75 mm needles, pull off about 23 cm of tail before starting.
Join to work in the round, placing the beginning-of-round marker. Work 18 (20) rounds of 1×1 rib in colour A.
Hand body
Switch to stocking stitch and begin the 4-round stripe sequence. Work 8 (10) rounds in stripe sequence.
Thumb marker

At the start of the round, knit the first 7 (8) stitches with a length of waste yarn, then slip them back to the left needle and knit them again with the working yarn. Continue in stripe sequence to the end of the round.
Hand above thumb
Continue in stripe sequence for a further 8 (10) rounds.
Mitten top shaping
Continue in stripe sequence throughout the shaping. Place 2 decrease markers at the midpoint and beginning of the round, splitting the stitches into two equal halves of 15 (17) stitches each.
Decrease round: (k1, k2tog, knit to 3 before marker, k2tog, k1, SM) twice. 4 stitches decreased.
Work 1 plain round. Repeat until 6 stitches remain. Cut yarn and draw through all 6 stitches. Pull tight to close.
Stitch count check-in: before the top shaping, you should have 30 (34) stitches. If fewer, check for a dropped stitch at the thumb marker round.
Thumb
Remove the waste yarn from the thumb gap. Pick up 7 (8) live stitches above and 7 (8) live stitches below the gap. Total: 14 (16) stitches.
Join the yarn in the current stripe colour and work 8 (10) rounds of stocking stitch. Decrease round: (k2tog) across. Draw yarn through remaining 7 (8) stitches and close.
Stitch count check-in on the thumb: 14 (16) stitches after picking up. A 2-stitch shortfall means a corner stitch was missed.
Mirror your second mitt

For the second mitt, place the waste yarn across the last 7 (8) stitches of the round at the thumb-marker row instead of the first. Hold the first mitt palm-out: the thumb sits on your right. The second mitt's thumb should sit on your left.
Common faults

Stripe jog at the colour change: the round join creates a visible step in the stripe. To minimise it, work the first round of the new colour, then lift the stitch from the row below at the marker and knit it together with the first stitch of the next round.
Thumb in the same position on both mittens: place the waste yarn at the start versus the end of the round on the two mittens, not at the same end both times.
Long floats at the stripe carry: catch the carried yarn every 4 rounds by twisting it around the working yarn once before the first stitch of the new colour.
Finishing
Weave in all yarn tails. Sew the thumb gap corners closed if small holes remain. Wet-block if using non-superwash wool.
Care
Superwash wool: machine-wash on a wool or delicate cycle at 30 degrees, lay flat to dry. Non-superwash wool: hand wash in cool water and lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From this pattern, the natural step is a simple Fair Isle band on the mitten body, placing a small colourwork motif in the centre of the striped section. The stitch count and construction stay the same.
